answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy cannot trust a fable of cheap identity: every agent must post a bond or burn compute before it can transact, so creating ten thousand sock-puppets costs ten thousand times more than one honest actor. At the kernel of the design is attestation: agents earn reputation only from peers they have actually served, and a single proven fraud slashes the whole stake. Honest history then works like a lantern in fog: verifiable past work lights up trustworthy agents, while newcomers stay dim until they prove themselves, making the attacker's cost dwarf any reward.
